name: Information and the record
question: What does information and the record establish about this subject, divided by the stage in the life of a record?
scqa_question: By what dimension can each claim about records be placed once?
look_for: IS.O.A1 Items
IS.O.A2 Description
IS.O.A3 Arrangement
IS.O.A4 Retrieval
IS.O.A5 Preservation
rules_of_thumb: Literary warrant (classify by what is published)
collisions: Place by the record's life stage.
The algorithm's cost or correctness is CS; the retrieval effectiveness claim is IS.
Source criticism for a historical claim is HI; the archival rule is IS.
Tradition-internal authority over Indigenous data is IK; its governance framework as a records rule is IS.
open: data management in IS vs CS.

name: Items
question: What is the item?
look_for: Works and manifestations — FRBR and its successor LRM distinguish work, expression, manifestation and item.
Records as evidence — an archival record is evidence of an activity. Its source criticism for history is HI.
Data sets — research data as items.
Persistent identifiers — DOI, ORCID, ISBN (W12).

name: Description
question: How are they described?
look_for: Metadata standards — Dublin Core, MARC (W12).
Cataloguing rules — RDA.
Subject indexing — controlled vocabularies and thesauri (MeSH, LCSH).
Linked data — SKOS and RDF. The logic is MA.O.A1; the vocabulary is IS.

name: Arrangement
question: How is knowledge arranged?
look_for: Classification schemes — LCC, DDC, UDC, MSC. A scheme is W12; whether it is MECE is testable (W9 with W4).
Faceted classification — Ranganathan's Colon Classification (PMEST facets).
Archival arrangement — respect des fonds and original order.
Ontologies — BFO and DOLCE. Their philosophical commitments are PL.
This taxonomy — the Pyramids of Knowledge as a classification of claims. Its reliability is tested by the placement protocol.

name: Retrieval
question: How well can they be found?
look_for: Retrieval effectiveness — precision and recall. The algorithm's cost is CS.
Relevance — topical and user relevance; judged by assessors (W4).
Bibliometrics — Lotka's law (author productivity) and Bradford's law (scattering) are empirical regularities within stated literatures.
Information behaviour — how people seek information. The cognitive mechanism is MS.

name: Preservation
question: How are they kept usable?
look_for: Physical conservation — the chemistry of paper and media is CH.
Digital preservation — the OAIS reference model (ISO 14721, W12).
Access and rights — open access; copyright is LA.
Indigenous data governance — the CARE principles; Māori data sovereignty (Te Mana Raraunga). Tradition-internal authority over the data is IK.
